newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT-Viacom to issue Blockbuster stock.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Viacom to issue Blockbuster stock.

text.p: Viacom Inc said it plans to issue a new class of stock that will track the performance of its Blockbuster unit. Viacom will retain the majority of the new class of stock. A full text of its statement follows.
Viacom pursuing initial public offering of stock to track performance of Blockbuster; Bill Fields to resign
Business Editors

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--April 22, 1997--Viacom Inc. (Amex: VIA and VIAB) announced today that, after studying several alternatives over the last few months, it has decided to pursue the public offering of shares of a new class of Viacom common stock that will track the performance of the Company's retail-based Blockbuster unit.
The Company plans to make the initial public offering, which will represent a minority of the new class, in early 1998. Proceeds from any sales of tracking stock shares will be used to repay debt.

Sumner M. Redstone, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Viacom, said, "Issuing a tracking stock will enable us to raise equity capital to reduce our debt, will provide an attractive opportunity for investors interested in Blockbuster and will make it possible for shareholders to better capture the value of all of Viacom's businesses. Viacom intends to retain a significant shareholding in the tracking stock reflecting our continued belief in Blockbuster's prospects. At the same time, the implementation of this strategy will leave Viacom with a great deal of financial flexibility."

Viacom also stated that, while it expects that Blockbuster's first quarter earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) will be down between 15% to 20% compared with the same quarter last year because of the inferior quality of video releases in the period and short term dislocations resulting from the move from Ft. Lauderdale to Dallas, the Company remains confident that Blockbuster will resume earnings growth in the second half of 1997.
Mr. Redstone added, "Each step being taken with respect to Blockbuster will result in that renewed growth."

Viacom also announced that, by mutual agreement , Bill Fields is resigning from his post as Chairman and Chief Executive of the Blockbuster Entertainment Group. The Company said it expects to announce shortly the selection, from among several highly qualified candidates, of an executive with the capabilities to lead Blockbuster under the new structure created by the proposed publicly traded security. In the interim, Blockbuster's operations will report to Mr. Redstone and Viacom Deputy Chairman, Tom Dooley.

Mr. Redstone said: "Bill Fields brought his long-time retailing perspectives to Blockbuster and helped us refine its operational focus and move the business to the next level as a separately reported entity. Together, we made enormous strides in a short period of time and his insights have been ingrained into Blockbuster's operations. We thank him for his contributions and wish him well."

Mr. Fields said: "In joining Blockbuster and becoming part of the Viacom team, I had the privilege of working with one of the most outstanding groups of executives anywhere. I continue to see a bright future for Blockbuster as a leader in family entertainment retailing and I am proud of the great progress we made in strengthening its operations and positioning it for continued growth. Nevertheless, it is clear to me that general retailing is in my blood and it is time for me to return to the industry where I spent my whole career."

Blockbuster is the market leader in the $20 billion home video industry and a major player in the music retailing field. At year-end 1996, Viacom's Blockbuster Entertainment Group comprised more than 5,300 domestic and international video stores in 24 countries and approximately 500 music stores. The Company's video and music store operations reported revenues of $3.54 billion and EBITDA of $775 million in 1996.

Viacom Inc. is one of the world's largest entertainment and publishing companies and a leading force in nearly every segment of the international media marketplace. The operations of Viacom include Blockbuster video and music, MTV Networks, Paramount Parks, Paramount Pictures, Paramount Television, Showtime Networks, Simon & Schuster, radio and television stations, and movie screens in 11 countries. Viacom also has a majority interest in Spelling Entertainment Group, as well as a half-interest in Comedy Central, and USA Networks, including the Sci-Fi Channel. National Amusements, Inc., a closely held corporation which operates approximately 1,100 screens in the U.S., the U.K. and South America, is the parent company of Viacom. More information about Viacom is available at the Company's Web site located at http://www.viacom.com. -0-
